text: Rethink archiving: what is an archived idea, and do we need it at all?
description:
Today (2026-10-17): 'archived' is a status; writeIdea moves the file to archived-ideas/ and default lists, search and proposals skip it. A separate archived boolean is redundant (never true in ideas/). All 10 archived ideas have zero connections — mostly merge_ideas leftovers, so archiving is effectively a soft delete. Meanwhile 538 of 809 active ideas are finished (implemented/cancelled) and are what actually clutters the graph. (Earlier "revise idea archiving", 827cb5c7, was cancelled for lacking a concrete requirement; this is that requirement.)

Problems:
- Archived mixes two axes: outcome (implemented/cancelled/failed) and liveness. Archiving overwrites the outcome. → archived should be a flag beside the status (stored-format change → migration).
- Merged ideas are redirects, not archive: "merged into X" should resolve old IDs (commits reference them), not be disconnected nodes.

Candidate meaning of archived: a settled, finished subtree — frozen (text/status/connections incl. incoming edges not editable; explicit unarchive possible), shown compressed, archivable only as a whole finished subtree. Still visible to dedupe, lessons lookup, and commit history; out of prioritization, default lists and rendering.

Alternative (leaning): if subtree compression is a cache available for any finished subtree (see the summary-cache idea), archiving loses its compressing job; what remains is freeze + hide, and hide is a view filter. Then drop archiving entirely and keep only merge redirects.

Open questions: does a finished child still absorb a share of its parent's value (archiving would shift open siblings' priorities)? Who archives and when (agent proposes, human confirms)? Can an archived idea gain new parents? Is a cancelled idea archivable immediately even with open children?

status.comment: Felix (2026-10-17): wants to keep the thoughts, cannot decide now. Decision: keep archiving as freeze+compress, or drop it in favor of a 'hide finished' view filter plus merge redirects.
